questions.q: What are the four generic tests dbt ships with out of the box?
options: not_null, unique, accepted_values, and relationships
not_null, unique, primary_key, and foreign_key
select, insert, update, and delete
staging, intermediate, marts, and exposures
questions.explain: These four ship with dbt itself and can be attached to any column via YAML — no custom SQL required.

questions.q: In schema.yml, how do you supply the target model and column for a `relationships` test?
options: With an `arguments:` block specifying `to` (the referenced model) and `field` (the column to match)
By writing a custom .sql file in the tests/ directory
Relationships tests cannot take any arguments in dbt
By adding a foreign key constraint directly in the warehouse
questions.explain: Parameterized tests like relationships and accepted_values take an arguments: block; simple tests like unique and not_null are listed by name alone.

questions.q: What is actually happening 'under the hood' when dbt runs a generic test?
options: It compiles to a select statement that returns the rows violating the assertion — zero rows means the test passes
dbt calls an external validation API for every column
It permanently deletes any row that fails the assertion
It only checks the column's data type, never its actual values
questions.explain: Every generic test is fundamentally a select query; if it returns any rows, those rows are the specific failures.

questions.q: What does the dbt Catalog's Test Status lens show, according to this lesson?
options: Each model node in the lineage graph with a colored badge for its latest test status (Pass, Error, Fail, Warn, Skipped)
A list of every user who has run a test in the last 30 days
The exact dollar cost of running each test
A random sample of untested columns
questions.explain: The Test Status lens overlays test health directly onto the real lineage graph, so a failure is visible right where it happened in the pipeline.

questions.q: Why does a non-zero test failure count matter for CI/CD, according to this lesson?
options: A failing test causes `dbt test` to return a non-zero exit code, which a CI/CD pipeline checks to decide whether a pull request is safe to merge
CI/CD pipelines ignore dbt test results entirely
It only matters for singular tests, not generic tests
A failing test automatically reverts the last git commit
questions.explain: The exit code is what makes dbt tests actionable in automation — CI/CD gates a merge on that code, not on someone manually reading logs.
